title: Psalms Chapter 142 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 142 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 142 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 142.

questions.question: Who is the author of Psalms 142 according to the chapter heading?
questions.correctAnswer: David
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:1 states it is a Maschil of David, indicating David as the author.

questions.question: Where was David when he made the prayer recorded in Psalms 142?
questions.correctAnswer: In the cave
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:1 states that this prayer was made when David was in the cave.

questions.question: What did David do with his voice according to Psalms 142:1?
questions.correctAnswer: He made supplication
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:1 says David cried unto the LORD with his voice and made his supplication.

questions.question: What did David 'pour out' before the LORD in Psalms 142:2?
questions.correctAnswer: His complaint
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:2 states David poured out his complaint before the LORD.

questions.question: What did David show before the LORD in Psalms 142:2?
questions.correctAnswer: His trouble
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:2 says David shewed before the LORD his trouble.

questions.question: According to Psalms 142:3, what was overwhelmed within David?
questions.correctAnswer: His spirit
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:3 states that when David's spirit was overwhelmed within him, the LORD knew his path.

questions.question: Who knew David's path when his spirit was overwhelmed, according to Psalms 142:3?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:3 says 'then thou knewest my path,' referring to the LORD.

questions.question: What did David say was laid privily in the way he walked in Psalms 142:3?
questions.correctAnswer: A snare
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:3 mentions that in the way David walked, they privily laid a snare for him.

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 142:4, David looked on his left hand and found no man to know him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:4 states David looked on his right hand, not left, and found no man to know him.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 142:5, David called the LORD his refuge and portion.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:5 says David cried unto the LORD and said He is his refuge and portion.

questions.question: Who did David ask to deliver him from his persecutors in Psalms 142:6?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:6 says David cried unto the LORD asking for deliverance from persecutors.

questions.question: What reason does David give for needing deliverance from persecutors in Psalms 142:6?
options: They are enemies of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They are stronger than I
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:6 states the persecutors are stronger than David, which is why he asks for deliverance.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 142:7 says the righteous shall compass David about.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:7 clearly states that the righteous shall compass David about.

questions.question: What does David want to do after his soul is brought out of prison according to Psalms 142:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Praise God's name
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:7 states David wants to praise the LORD's name after deliverance.

questions.question: In Psalms 142, which action comes first?
options: David crying unto the LORD with his voice
David asking for deliverance from persecutors
David looking on his right hand
questions.correctAnswer: David crying unto the LORD with his voice
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 142:1, David first cried unto the LORD with his voice before pouring out his complaint (v2), looking on his right hand (v4), or asking for deliverance (v6).

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 142 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 142 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 142:4, what did David find when he looked to his right hand?
options: No man that would know him
questions.correctAnswer: No man that would know him
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:4 states that when David looked on his right hand, there was no man that would know him, emphasizing his isolation and lack of support.

questions.question: How does Psalms 142:5 describe the LORD in relation to the psalmist's life?
options: As his refuge and portion in the land of the living
questions.correctAnswer: As his refuge and portion in the land of the living
questions.explanation: In Psalms 142:5, David calls the LORD his refuge and portion, indicating trust and reliance on God as his protector and provider in life.

questions.question: What reason does David give in Psalms 142:6 for crying out to the LORD?
options: Because he is brought very low and persecuted
Because he wants to give thanks
questions.correctAnswer: Because he is brought very low and persecuted
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:6 explains that David cries to the LORD due to being brought very low and needing deliverance from his persecutors, showing humility and dependence on God.

questions.question: What does David ask God to do in Psalms 142:7 so that he may praise God's name?
options: Bring his soul out of prison
questions.correctAnswer: Bring his soul out of prison
questions.explanation: David petitions in Psalms 142:7 for God to bring his soul out of prison so he can praise God's name, highlighting the link between deliverance and worship.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 142:4, refuge failed David because no man cared for his soul.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:4 explicitly states that refuge failed David and no man cared for his soul, showing his deep sense of abandonment.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 142:5-6, how does trusting God as refuge help a believer facing persecution?
options: It provides a source of strength and hope amid overwhelming opposition
It guarantees immediate removal of all troubles
It makes the believer invincible to enemies
It removes the need for prayer
questions.correctAnswer: It provides a source of strength and hope amid overwhelming opposition
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 reveal that trusting God as refuge helps the believer find strength and hope even when persecutors are stronger, teaching reliance on God in hardship.

questions.question: What does Psalms 142:3 reveal about the nature of the trouble David faced?
options: He was overwhelmed and enemies laid a secret snare
He was physically weak from illness
He was confused about his path
He was surrounded by joyful friends
questions.correctAnswer: He was overwhelmed and enemies laid a secret snare
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:3 states that David's spirit was overwhelmed and enemies secretly laid a snare in his path, indicating hidden dangers and emotional distress.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 142:2, David kept his trouble private and did not share it with the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:2 says David poured out his complaint and showed his trouble before the LORD, demonstrating open prayer and honesty with God.

questions.question: How does Psalms 142:7 suggest that deliverance from hardship affects a believer's relationships?
options: The righteous will surround and support the believer
The believer will be completely isolated
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous will surround and support the believer
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:7 indicates that once God deals bountifully with the believer, the righteous will compass him about, showing restoration of fellowship.

questions.question: What is the practical lesson about prayer learned from Psalms 142:1 and 142:6?
options: Persistently crying out to God in times of distress expresses trust and humility
Prayer should only be used when all else fails
Prayer is unnecessary when one feels low
questions.correctAnswer: Persistently crying out to God in times of distress expresses trust and humility
questions.explanation: Verses 1 and 6 show David crying out with his voice and asking God to attend to his cry, teaching believers to humbly and persistently pray in hardship.

questions.question: What does Psalms 142:5 teach about the believer’s portion in life?
options: God Himself is the believer’s portion and refuge
Material wealth is the believer’s portion
Success and honor are the believer’s portion
questions.correctAnswer: God Himself is the believer’s portion and refuge
questions.explanation: In Psalms 142:5, David identifies the LORD as his refuge and portion, teaching that God alone satisfies and sustains the believer.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 142:6 reveals that David felt equal in strength to his persecutors.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:6 states that David cried to God because his persecutors were stronger than he, showing his humility and dependence on divine help.

questions.question: How does Psalms 142:4-5 illustrate the shift from despair to hope in prayer?
options: From feeling abandoned by man to trusting God as refuge
From trusting enemies to trusting friends
questions.correctAnswer: From feeling abandoned by man to trusting God as refuge
questions.explanation: Verse 4 shows David's despair over no human help, while verse 5 transitions to affirming God as refuge, teaching reliance on God beyond human support.

questions.question: What does Psalms 142:3 teach about God's awareness of our path during difficult times?
options: God knows our path even when our spirit is overwhelmed
God is unaware of hidden snares
We walk our path alone without God's knowledge
Our path is always easy and clear
questions.correctAnswer: God knows our path even when our spirit is overwhelmed
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:3 says "then thou knewest my path," showing God's intimate knowledge and care even in overwhelming circumstances.

questions.question: What does Psalms 142:7 imply about God's character in dealing with the psalmist?
options: God deals bountifully with the psalmist
God is indifferent to the psalmist's plight
questions.correctAnswer: God deals bountifully with the psalmist
questions.explanation: Verse 7 promises that God shall deal bountifully, indicating His generous and gracious nature toward those who seek Him.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 142 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 142.

questions.question: What is the psalmist's request in Psalms 142:7?
options: Bring my soul out of prison
Give me strength to fight my enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Bring my soul out of prison
questions.explanation: The psalmist petitions God to bring his soul out of prison so that he may praise His name, as stated explicitly in Psalms 142:7.

questions.question: According to Psalms 142:7, who will surround the psalmist when God deals bountifully with him?
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:7 says 'the righteous shall compass me about' indicating that those who are righteous will surround the psalmist when God is bountiful to him.

questions.question: What literary device is prominent in Psalms 142, especially seen in the parallelism between verses 1 and 2?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: The psalm shows parallelism in verses 1 and 2 where the psalmist repeats the act of crying and pouring out complaints before the LORD, a typical Hebrew poetic device (Psalms 142:1-2).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God being the refuge and portion of the faithful as stated in Psalms 142:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 6:18
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:18 speaks of the hope set before us as an anchor of the soul, a concept echoing God as refuge and portion in Psalms 142:5.

questions.question: In Psalms 142:3, what does the psalmist say about his spirit?
options: It was lifted up in joy
It was renewed by the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: It was overwhelmed within him
questions.explanation: The psalmist states that his spirit was overwhelmed within him, indicating deep distress as recorded in Psalms 142:3.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated as 'prison' in Psalms 142:7, and what does it signify in the psalmist's context?
options: Sakar meaning bondage; signifies physical imprisonment
Chalal meaning valley; signifies a place of despair
Asir meaning prison; signifies a metaphorical state of distress
questions.correctAnswer: Asir meaning prison; signifies a metaphorical state of distress
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Asir' used here means prison and in this context symbolizes the psalmist's deep distress and feeling trapped (Psalms 142:7).

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 142:4, the psalmist found many companions who cared for his soul.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 142:4 explicitly states that no man cared for the psalmist's soul; refuge failed him and he found no one who knew him.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book contains a similar theme of God as refuge and protector in times of trouble, akin to Psalms 142:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah
questions.explanation: Isaiah frequently portrays God as refuge and strength for the afflicted, echoing the theme in Psalms 142:5.

questions.question: What does the psalmist mean by saying 'Thou art my refuge and my portion in the land of the living' in Psalms 142:5?
options: God is the psalmist's inheritance and protector during life
God will grant him land and possessions
He will become a leader among the living
He will live forever in the land
questions.correctAnswer: God is the psalmist's inheritance and protector during life
questions.explanation: The verse expresses that God is both the shelter and portion—the inheritance and sustenance—for the psalmist in his earthly life (Psalms 142:5).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the idea of deliverance from spiritual imprisonment similar to Psalms 142:7?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:25-26 describes Paul and Silas being miraculously delivered from prison, reflecting the theme of deliverance in Psalms 142:7.

questions.question: In Psalms 142:6, why does the psalmist ask God to deliver him from persecutors?
options: Because they are stronger than he
questions.correctAnswer: Because they are stronger than he
questions.explanation: The psalmist acknowledges the strength of his persecutors and asks for deliverance because they are stronger than he is (Psalms 142:6).

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 142 is an example of a Maschil, a song meant for teaching or contemplation.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 142 is introduced as a Maschil of David, a type of psalm intended for instruction or contemplation (Psalms 142:1).

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'with my voice' repeated in Psalms 142:1?
options: Emphasizes the urgency and earnestness of the prayer
Indicates the psalmist’s inability to speak silently
Shows a poetic redundancy with no deeper meaning
Refers to a musical instrument accompanying the voice
questions.correctAnswer: Emphasizes the urgency and earnestness of the prayer
questions.explanation: The repetition in Psalms 142:1 highlights the earnestness and intensity of David's prayer in his distress.

questions.question: How does Psalms 142:3 foreshadow later New Testament teachings about spiritual warfare?
options: By mentioning secret snares laid by adversaries
By describing physical battles with enemies
questions.correctAnswer: By mentioning secret snares laid by adversaries
questions.explanation: The mention of snares in Psalms 142:3 foreshadows the spiritual warfare themes found in Ephesians 6:11 where believers are urged to be aware of the devil’s schemes.

questions.question: Which cultural or historical context best explains the setting of Psalms 142 as a 'Prayer when he was in the cave'?
options: David hiding from Saul during his flight
questions.correctAnswer: David hiding from Saul during his flight
questions.explanation: The superscription in Psalms 142 points to David praying while hiding in a cave, likely during his flight from King Saul, a well-known historical context (Psalms 142:1).

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 142 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 142 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What kind of prayer is Psalm 142 described as in its opening verse?
options: A prayer when David was in the cave
questions.correctAnswer: A prayer when David was in the cave
questions.explanation: Psalm 142:1 explicitly states it is 'A Prayer when he was in the cave,' indicating the context of David’s supplication.

questions.question: What does David do in Psalm 142:2 that reveals his approach to God in times of trouble?
options: He pours out his complaint before God
questions.correctAnswer: He pours out his complaint before God
questions.explanation: Psalm 142:2 states, 'I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble', showing David’s openness and honesty in prayer.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Psalm 142:3 when it says 'then thou knewest my path'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's omniscience
questions.explanation: Psalm 142:3 acknowledges God's knowledge of David’s path, illustrating God's omniscience—the attribute of all-knowing.

questions.question: What is the situation described by David in Psalm 142:4 regarding human help?
options: No man cared for his soul
questions.correctAnswer: No man cared for his soul
questions.explanation: Psalm 142:4 states 'no man cared for my soul,' highlighting David’s isolation and lack of human help.

questions.question: Which doctrine about God is conveyed in Psalm 142:5 where David calls the LORD his refuge and portion?
options: Doctrine of God as a refuge and sustainer
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of God as a refuge and sustainer
questions.explanation: Psalm 142:5 presents God as 'my refuge and my portion,' emphasizing God’s role as protector and provider, foundational to Christian doctrine of God’s care.

questions.question: What urgent request does David make in Psalm 142:6 regarding his condition and enemies?
options: To deliver him from persecutors stronger than he
questions.correctAnswer: To deliver him from persecutors stronger than he
questions.explanation: Psalm 142:6 says, 'deliver me from my persecutors; for they are stronger than I,' showing David’s plea for divine intervention against overwhelming foes.

questions.question: What future hope does David express in Psalm 142:7 after deliverance?
questions.correctAnswer: To praise God's name
questions.explanation: Psalm 142:7 states, 'that I may praise thy name,' indicating David’s hope to worship God freely after rescue.

questions.question: How does Psalm 142 depict human loneliness in the context of divine help?
options: Loneliness is a test of faith
Human refuge often fails, but God remains faithful
questions.correctAnswer: Human refuge often fails, but God remains faithful
questions.explanation: Psalm 142:4 shows no man cared for David’s soul and refuge failed him, but subsequent verses reveal God as the true refuge, highlighting human insufficiency versus divine faithfulness.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is emphasized by David’s declaration ‘Thou art my refuge and my portion’ in light of his distress?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence and protection
questions.explanation: Psalm 142:5 highlights God as refuge and portion, emphasizing His providential care and protective nature toward the believer.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do Psalms 142:3 and 142:6 provide regarding human weakness and divine awareness?
options: Human spirit is strong enough without God
God knows the overwhelmed spirit and is called to deliver the lowly
Persecutors are more powerful than God
questions.correctAnswer: God knows the overwhelmed spirit and is called to deliver the lowly
questions.explanation: Psalm 142:3 acknowledges God’s knowledge of David’s overwhelmed spirit; Psalm 142:6 shows David’s plea for deliverance, indicating divine awareness coupled with human dependence.

questions.question: How does Psalm 142 reflect the doctrine of sanctification when it says 'the righteous shall compass me about' in verse 7?
options: Sanctification involves community of the righteous surrounding the believer
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves community of the righteous surrounding the believer
questions.explanation: Psalm 142:7 indicates that after deliverance, the righteous surround the psalmist, suggesting sanctification is nurtured within the community of God’s people.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that prayers in desperate situations show human weakness rather than divine efficacy. What does Psalms 142:1-7 actually teach about the nature of prayer and God’s response?
options: Prayer is a cry to a knowing and powerful refuge who delivers
Prayer is a sign of divine abandonment
Prayer is only for formal worship
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer is a cry to a knowing and powerful refuge who delivers
questions.explanation: Psalm 142:1-7 shows David crying out with honesty and trust to God, who knows his path and is his refuge, indicating prayer as both realistic about human weakness and confident in God’s power (cf. Hebrews 4:16).

questions.question: What does the phrase 'I poured out my complaint before him' in Psalm 142:2 teach about the believer's access to God in suffering?
options: Believers have direct, open access to express their troubles to God
Believers should only praise, not complain
Believers rely on others to express their complaints
questions.correctAnswer: Believers have direct, open access to express their troubles to God
questions.explanation: Psalm 142:2 demonstrates that David directly and openly pours out his complaints to God, illustrating the doctrine of direct access to God in prayer (cf. Romans 8:26).

questions.question: How does the imagery of 'brought very low' and 'deliver me from my persecutors' in Psalm 142:6 relate to the biblical understanding of human sin and suffering?
options: Human lowliness often results from sin and persecution, requiring divine rescue
Human suffering is always punishment without hope
Persecution is a sign of divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: Human lowliness often results from sin and persecution, requiring divine rescue
questions.explanation: Psalm 142:6 portrays human lowliness and persecution, consistent with biblical teaching that sin and spiritual opposition cause suffering, necessitating God’s deliverance (cf. 2 Corinthians 12:9).

questions.question: What does the reference to 'prison' in Psalm 142:7 symbolize in the broader redemptive narrative of Scripture?
options: Spiritual bondage from which God delivers His people
A metaphor for wealth and comfort
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual bondage from which God delivers His people
questions.explanation: Psalm 142:7’s call to bring the soul out of prison typifies spiritual captivity, foreshadowing God’s redemptive deliverance seen in the Exodus and ultimately in Christ’s salvation (cf. Isaiah 61:1).
